finding.claim: Big5 lead-byte range is 0xA1-0xFE, wider than the server's 0xA1-0xF9. A Buffer parameter containing bytes 0xFA, 0x5C, 0x27 is treated by the driver as one multibyte char (0xFA + trail 0x5C) copied verbatim, then the quote is escaped with an inserted backslash. The server reads 0xFA as a single byte, so the 0x5C escapes the inserted backslash and the quote closes the literal. SQL injection, conditional on the server range being 0xA1-0xF9 (not verified against server source).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled bytes in a Buffer value passed as a ? parameter to query() in text protocol, on a connection whose negotiated collation charset is big5 (lib/io/packet-output-stream.js:85).
finding.sink: SQL text sent to the server inside a _BINARY '...' literal (lib/cmd/encoder/text-encoder.js:32-34).

trace.note: Buffer.isBuffer branch selected for the parameter
writeBufferEscape bound to writeBufferEscapeMb when getMbRecognizer('big5') returns a recognizer
NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES shortcut not taken in default backslash mode, so the mb walk runs
mbLen is 2, so the pair is copied verbatim with no escape inserted
next byte 0x27 is QUOTE, so a backslash is inserted before it

finding.guards_checked: NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES fast path (packet-output-stream.js:684) bypassed in default mode. Lone-head escape (lines 706-713) does not apply because the pair is valid per the driver. Quote escaping at 715-718 applies after the verbatim pair, so the injected backslash is the only escape. Server-range assumption is unverified.

finding.claim: Server-supplied redirect_url makes the driver open a new connection to a server-chosen host with the original user's password. The password is inherited via Object.assign when the URL has no password, so credentials go to an attacker-chosen host.
finding.source: Server-controlled redirect_url in an OK packet or session-state change. Requires a malicious server, or a MITM on a non-TLS connection.
finding.sink: New Connection authenticates to the attacker-chosen host using this.opts.password (lib/connection.js:1633-1636), which can disclose the native password hash or, over TLS with a clear-text auth switch, the plaintext password.

trace.note: case redirect_url from session state change calls info.redirect(value, ...)
gated only by this.opts.permitRedirect and a non-empty value
allowed when receiveQueue length <= 1 and not in a transaction
host and port taken from the server-supplied URL
user and password overridden only if present in the URL
Object.assign({}, this.opts, redirectOpts) keeps the original password
conn.connect() authenticates to the new host with those credentials

finding.guards_checked: Same-host skip (lib/connection.js:1621) only. TLS verification (connection-options.js:107-110, connection.js:970-976) uses servername = new host, so a host with a valid certificate for its own name passes. The clear-text auth plugin requires TLS (authentication.js:203). Did not verify whether the server must advertise a client capability to send redirect_url.
